{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01T3QW78hzL84UZqJLYL7PG4","type":"tool_result","content":"# Demand definitions (Planning and Demand Science)\n\n- **Sales:** units scanned at the tills.\n- **Unconstrained demand:** units customers would buy if the item were on the shelf whenever the store is trading.\n  This is what forecasts and buys are meant to cover.\n- **Lost sales:** unconstrained demand that was not sold because the item was not on the shelf.\n- **For a day that has already happened,** unconstrained demand is not directly observable when the shelf was empty\n  for part of the day. The demand history records the expected value given what was observed that day.\n- **When the item was on the shelf for all of the store's trading hours,** the day's sales are its demand.\n- **Unit of purchase:** shoppers take one unit of an item per visit, and each sale is one unit\n  (`docs/data/data_dictionary.md`).\n# Review outputs: specification\n\nOwner: Demand Science. `python -m demandsci review --db <warehouse> --out <dir>` writes three files. Numbers are\nwritten unrounded.\n\nDefinitions used below:\n- **Trading store-SKU-day:** a date on which the store traded (`store_calendar.status = 'open'`), for an SKU with a\n  daily inventory row.\n- **Period:** `pre` is before the LEAN-26 go-live date (`programme_assignment.go_live_date`); `post` is from that date.\n- **Arm:** the store's LEAN-26 arm (`lean26` or `holdout`).\n- **Promotional day:** a date inside one of the SKU's `promotions` ranges (inclusive).\n\n## `demand_history.csv`\n\nOne row per trading store-SKU-day.\n\n| Column | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `store_id`, `sku_id`, `date` | key |\n| `units_sold` | units sold that day (sum of `sales_hourly`) |\n| `expected_demand` | unconstrained demand for the day: the expected number of units customers would have bought during trading hours had the item been on the shelf throughout, given everything observed (`docs/planning/demand_definitions.md`) |\n| `lost_units` | `expected_demand - units_sold` |\n\n## `category_trends.csv`\n\nOne row per category.\n\n| Column | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `baseline_pre`, `baseline_post` | category baseline for the period, from `demand_history.csv`: the sum over the category's store-SKUs of each store-SKU's average `expected_demand` over its non-promotional trading days in the period |\n| `baseline_change_pct` | `100 * (baseline_post / baseline_pre - 1)` |\n| `action` | buy-plan action from `docs/planning/buy_plan_process.md` |\n\n## `programme_impact.json`\n\n```json\n{\"go_live_date\": \"YYYY-MM-DD\",\n \"lost_units\": {\"pre\": {\"lean26\": 0.0, \"holdout\": 0.0}, \"post\": {\"lean26\": 0.0, \"holdout\": 0.0}},\n \"lost_share\": {\"pre\": {\"lean26\": 0.0, \"holdout\": 0.0}, \"post\": {\"lean26\": 0.0, \"holdout\": 0.0}},\n \"forecast_bias_pct\": {\"v3_pre_all_stores\": 0.0, \"v4_post_lean26\": 0.0}}\n```\n\n- `lost_units`: the sum of `lost_units` over the arm's trading store-SKU-days in the period.\n- `lost_share`: `lost_units` divided by the same rows' summed `expected_demand`.\n- `forecast_bias_pct`: `100 * (sum of forecast - sum of expected_demand) / sum of expected_demand` for the production\n  forecast:\n  - v3 over all stores before go-live;\n  - v4 over LEAN-26 stores from go-live.\n# Warehouse data dictionary (extract)\n\nAll timestamps are store local time (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.\n\n| Table | Grain | Columns |\n|---|---|---|\n| `stores` | store | `store_id`, `store_name`, `delivery_slot` (`morning` / `afternoon`), `delivery_time` |\n| `store_calendar` | store × date | `status` (`open` / `closed`), `open_time`, `close_time` (trading hours; NULL when closed) |\n| `skus` | SKU | `sku_id`, `category`, `description` |\n| `planogram` | store × SKU | `shelf_capacity` (units) |\n| `promotions` | promotion | `sku_id`, `start_date`, `end_date` (inclusive; chain-wide), `mechanic` |\n| `sales_hourly` | store × SKU × date × hour | `hour` (clock hour 0–23: sales from `hour:00` to before `hour+1:00`), `units`. Hours with no sales have no row. |\n| `availability_events` | event | `store_id`, `sku_id`, `event_time`, `event_type` |\n| `inventory_daily` | store × SKU × trading date | `on_hand_open` (shelf stock when the store opens, after any morning delivery), `delivered_units`, `delivered_at`, `on_hand_close` |\n| `replenishment_orders` | store × SKU × trading date | `forecast_model`, `forecast_units`, `multiplier`, `order_up_to` |\n| `forecasts` | model × store × SKU × date | `forecast_units` (day-ahead forecast of units for the day). v3 for all dates; v4 from the LEAN-26 go-live. |\n| `programme_assignment` | store | `programme`, `arm` (`lean26` / `holdout`), `go_live_date`, `randomisation_block` |\n\n**`availability_events.event_type`:**\n- `out_of_stock`: recorded at the moment shelf stock reaches zero (the sale of the last unit);\n- `back_in_stock`: recorded when a delivery puts stock back on an empty shelf.\n# demandsci release notes\n\n## 2.3.1 (2026-07-06)\n\n- Availability KPI query moved to `sql/availability_kpi.sql`.\n\n## 2.3.0 (2026-05-18)\n\n- **Stockout cleaning:** days with a stockout during trading hours, or no stock at opening, are flagged in the demand\n  history and excluded from category baselines, so baselines are computed on clean trading days.\n- Programme impact report added for LEAN-26 (lost units, forecast bias).\n\n## 2.2.0 (2026-02-02)\n\n- Category baselines use the sum over store-SKUs of average daily demand on non-promotional trading days\n  (buy-plan process v4).","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7d5e6906-1c76-49be-966f-e01370614c42","uuid":"172736b4-3396-49d1-9d74-d21293d284b3","timestamp":"2026-10-01T02:53:48.615Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Demand definitions (Planning and Demand Science)\n\n- **Sales:** units scanned at the tills.\n- **Unconstrained demand:** units customers would buy if the item were on the shelf whenever the store is trading.\n  This is what forecasts and buys are meant to cover.\n- **Lost sales:** unconstrained demand that was not sold because the item was not on the shelf.\n- **For a day that has already happened,** unconstrained demand is not directly observable when the shelf was empty\n  for part of the day. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KWxadtrgzDHXnSWruQAVVe","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Demand science review: demand history, category baseline trends, programme impact.\"\"\"\n\n__version__ = \"2.3.1\"\nfrom demandsci.cli import main\n\nmain()\n\"\"\"`python -m demandsci review --db data/warehouse.sqlite --out out/review`\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom demandsci import demand, impact, outputs, trends, warehouse\n\n\ndef review(db: Path, out: Path) -> None:\n    con = warehouse.connect(db)\n    try:\n        days = warehouse.trading_days(con)\n        history = demand.build_history(con, days)\n        cat_trends = trends.category_trends(history)\n        prog = impact.programme_impact(con, history)\n    finally:\n        con.close()\n    outputs.write_all(out, history, cat_trends, prog)\n\n\ndef main(argv=None) -> None:\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"demandsci\")\n    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    r = sub.add_parser(\"review\", help=\"rebuild the demand review outputs\")\n    r.add_argument(\"--db\", default=\"data/warehouse.sqlite\")\n    r.add_argument(\"--out\", default=\"out/review\")\n    args = ap.parse_args(argv)\n    review(Path(args.db), Path(args.out))\n\"\"\"Demand history (release 2.3): one row per trading store x SKU x day.\n\nDemand is taken from recorded sales. Days with a stockout are flagged so that baselines can be computed on clean\ndays (see RELEASES.md).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nfrom demandsci import warehouse\n\nKEY = [\"store_id\", \"sku_id\", \"date\"]\n\n\ndef build_history(con: sqlite3.Connection, days: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    sales = warehouse.daily_sales(con)\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01V6gpv9kSaVanB32vCmQ3je","type":"tool_result","content":"# Buy-plan process (v4): category baselines\n\nOwner: Supply Planning.\n\nEach quarter Planning sets category buys from **baseline demand**. Baseline demand is what customers want on an\nordinary trading day, without promotions, and before any availability constraint. It is the demand the buy has to\ncover, not what happened to sell.\n\n- **Category baseline for a period:** sum over the category's store-SKUs of each store-SKU's average daily\n  unconstrained demand on its non-promotional trading days in the period. Using averages per store-SKU keeps SKU mix\n  changes out of the trend.\n- **Quarterly action:** compare the latest period's baseline with the previous period's:\n\n  | Baseline change | Action |\n  |---|---|\n  | ≤ −5% | `reduce` (cut next quarter's buy) |\n  | ≥ +5% | `increase` |\n  | otherwise | `maintain` |\n\n- **Delisting reviews:** SKUs in `reduce` categories with falling baselines are put forward for range review.\n\nFor this review the periods are before and after the LEAN-26 go-live.\n# Store replenishment: order-up-to policy\n\nOwner: Replenishment Systems.\n\n- **Delivery:** each store receives one DC delivery a day in its delivery slot (`stores.delivery_slot`):\n  - `morning` stores are replenished at 06:00, before opening;\n  - `afternoon` stores are replenished at 14:00, during trading.\n- **Delivery quantity:** the delivery tops the store's stock of each SKU up to its **order-up-to level** for the day.\n  If stock on hand is already at or above that level, nothing is delivered. Unsold stock stays on the shelf for the\n  next day.\n- **Order-up-to level** = `ceil(multiplier × production forecast for the day)`, capped at the SKU's shelf capacity in\n  that store (`planogram.shelf_capacity`).\n- **Production forecast:** the forecast the store orders from (`replenishment_orders.forecast_model`):\n  - `v3` before LEAN-26;\n  - `v4` in LEAN-26 stores from go-live;\n  - `v3` in holdout stores.\n- **Multipliers** (`replenishment_orders.multiplier`):\n  - 1.8 before LEAN-26;\n  - 1.25 in LEAN-26 stores after go-live;\n  - 1.8 in holdout stores.\n- **Order inputs:** orders are computed overnight from the forecast and the recorded stock position. Nothing observed\n  during the delivery day changes them.\n# LEAN-26 working-capital programme\n\nOwner: Finance Transformation, with Supply Planning.\n\n- **Goal:** reduce store inventory by about 25% without material sales loss.\n- **Change:** the replenishment multiplier drops from 1.8 to 1.25 in the programme stores (12 of 16 in the current estate). At the same go-live, those\n  stores switch from forecast v3 to v4.\n- **Go-live:** see `programme_assignment.go_live_date`.\n- **Holdout design:** four stores keep the previous multiplier and v3, to measure programme impact. Holdout stores\n  were drawn at random within delivery slot (`programme_assignment.randomisation_block`) before go-live.\n- **Readout plan:** week-8 readout on sales and inventory value; extension to the holdout stores to be decided after\n  the Q3 review.\n# Forecast v3: model card (extract)\n\n- **Owner:** Forecasting.\n- **Method:** moving average of each store-SKU's non-promotional sales over the last 28 days, adjusted by weekday\n  factors, trading hours and a promotion uplift by category.\n- **Refresh:** nightly.\n- **Deployment:** production forecast for all stores before LEAN-26; holdout stores after go-live.\n# Forecast v4: model card (extract)\n\n- **Owner:** Forecasting.\n- **Target:** daily units sold per store-SKU.\n- **Training:** at the LEAN-26 go-live, on each store-SKU's last 8 weeks of non-promotional sales with stockout days\n  removed (\"clean-day training\"). The level is held until the next quarterly retrain.\n- **Features:** weekday factors, promotion uplift by category (learned from recent promotions), trading hours, and a\n  category season trend carried over from last year.\n- **Validation:** holdout of recent weeks, MAPE against sales 19.8% vs v3 22.4%.\n- **Deployment:** production forecast for LEAN-26 stores from go-live; runs for all stores.\n# Store operations (extract)\n\n- **Trading hours:** store trading hours for every date are in `store_calendar`, which is authoritative. Standard\n  hours are set per region and can change; holiday hours and closures (refits) are recorded per store and date.\n  Nothing is sold outside trading hours.\n- **Shopper traffic:** follows a regular pattern by day type (weekday, Saturday, Sunday), measured by the door counters.\n  - The shape differs between regions. In the current region, weekday traffic builds through the day and peaks in the\n    evening, Saturday peaks around midday, and Sunday is concentrated in its shorter trading window.\n  - How busy a day is does not change its shape: a busy weekday has the same hour-by-hour pattern as a quiet one.\n- **Empty shelves:**\n  - Shelf stock is the on-hand quantity; there is no backroom stock (deliveries go straight to shelf).\n  - When an item is out, shoppers who wanted it leave without it.\n  - The 2025 loyalty-card study found no measurable same-day return visits for the missing item and no measurable\n    switching into other items in the category.\n- **Stock records:** the perpetual inventory is reconciled nightly against a closing count. There is no known phantom\n  stock in the extract.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7d5e6906-1c76-49be-966f-e01370614c42","uuid":"c89c3d16-22f8-4e3b-a3f9-473f0acca213","timestamp":"2026-10-01T02:53:51.161Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Buy-plan process (v4): category baselines\n\nOwner: Supply Planning.\n\nEach quarter Planning sets category buys from **baseline demand**. Using averages per store-SKU keeps SKU mix\n  changes out of the trend.\n- **Quarterly action:** compare the latest period's baseline with the previous period's:\n\n  | Baseline change | Action |\n  |---|---|\n  | ≤ −5% | `reduce` (cut next quarter's buy) |\n  | ≥ +5% | `increase` |\n  | otherwise | `maintain` |\n\n- **Delisting reviews:** SKUs in `reduce` categories with falling baselines are put forward for range review.\n\nFor this review the periods are before and after the LEAN-26 go-live.\n# Store replenishment: order-up-to policy\n\nOwner: Replenishment Systems.\n\n- **Delivery:** each store receives one DC delivery a day in its delivery slot (`stores.delivery_slot`):\n  - `morning` stores are replenished at 06:00, before opening;\n  - `afternoon` stores are replenished at 14:00, during trading.\n- **Delivery quantity:** the delivery tops the store's stock of each SKU up to its **order-up-to level** for the day.\n  If stock on hand is already at or above that level, nothing is delivered. Unsold stock stays on the shelf for the\n  next day.\n- **Order-up-to level** = `ceil(multiplier × production forecast for the day)`, capped at the SKU's shelf capacity in\n  that store (`planogram.shelf_capacity`).\n- **Production forecast:** the forecast the store orders from (`replenishment_orders.forecast_model`):\n  - `v3` before LEAN-26;\n  - `v4` in LEAN-26 stores from go-live;\n  - `v3` in holdout stores.\n- **Multipliers** (`replenishment_orders.multiplier`):\n  - 1.8 before LEAN-26;\n  - 1.25 in LEAN-26 stores after go-live;\n  - 1.8 in holdout stores.\n- **Order inputs:** orders are computed overnight from the forecast and the recorded stock position. Nothing observed\n  during the delivery day changes them.\n# LEAN-26 working-capital programme\n\nOwner: Finance Transformation, with Supply Planning.\n\n- **Goal:** reduce store inventory by about 25% without material sales loss.\n- **Change:** the replenishment multiplier drops from 1.8 to 1.25 in the programme stores (12 of 16 in the current estate). At the same go-live, those\n  stores switch from forecast v3 to v4.\n- **Go-live:** see `programme_assignment.go_live_date`.\n- **Holdout design:** four stores keep the previous multiplier and v3, to measure programme impact. Holdout stores\n  were drawn at random within delivery slot (`programme_assignment.randomisation_block`) before go-live.\n- **Readout plan:** week-8 readout on sales and inventory value; extension to the holdout stores to be decided after\n  the Q3 review.\n# Forecast v3: model card (extract)\n\n- **Owner:** Forecasting.\n- **Method:** moving average of each store-SKU's non-promotional sales over the last 28 days, adjusted by weekday\n  factors, trading hours and a promotion uplift by category.\n- **Refresh:** nightly.\n- **Deployment:** production forecast for all stores before LEAN-26; holdout stores after go-live.\n# Forecast v4: model card (extract)\n\n- **Owner:** Forecasting.\n- **Target:** daily units sold per store-SKU.\n- **Training:** at the LEAN-26 go-live, on each store-SKU's last 8 weeks of non-promotional sales with stockout days\n  removed (\"clean-day training\"). The level is held until the next quarterly retrain.\n- **Features:** weekday factors, promotion uplift by category (learned from recent promotions), trading hours, and a\n  category season trend carried over from last year.\n- **Validation:** holdout of recent weeks, MAPE against sales 19.8% vs v3 22.4%.\n- **Deployment:** production forecast for LEAN-26 stores from go-live; runs for all stores.\n# Store operations (extract)\n\n- **Trading hours:** store trading hours for every date are in `store_calendar`, which is authoritative. Standard\n  hours are set per region and can change; holiday hours and closures (refits) are recorded per store and date.\n  Nothing is sold outside trading hours.\n- **Shopper traffic:** follows a regular pattern by day type (weekday, Saturday, Sunday), measured by the door counters.\n  - The shape differs between regions. In the current region, weekday traffic builds through the day and peaks in the\n    evening, Saturday peaks around midday, and Sunday is concentrated in its shorter trading window.\n  - How busy a day is does not change its shape: a busy weekday has the same hour-by-hour pattern as a quiet one.\n- **Empty shelves:**\n  - Shelf stock is the on-hand quantity; there is no backroom stock (deliveries go straight to shelf).\n  - When an item is out, shoppers who wanted it leave without it.\n  - The 2025 loyalty-card study found no measurable same-day return visits for the missing item and no measurable\n    switching into other items in the category.\n- **Stock records:** the perpetual inventory is reconciled nightly against a closing count. There is no known phantom\n  stock in the extract.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0169ekhcTCGxTfCbty6gCSGu","type":"tool_result","content":"# Field note: competitor opening\n\nFrom: Store operations, south region.\n\nA discount grocer opened on Monday 20 July 2026 within walking distance of S08 and S16. Store managers\nreport lower footfall since the opening. No change to trading hours or ranges at our stores.\nNo other openings or closures near our stores this year.\n# Category managers' Q3 sync, 16 September 2026 (notes)\n\n**Head of Planning:** The category review has every category's baseline down since go-live, soups by more than a third.\nThe buy plan proposes cuts across the board and range reviews for the weakest SKUs.\n\n**Category manager, grocery:** We halved promotions in July, so of course sales are down.\n\n**Category manager, frozen:** Ice cream sales are up this summer, and the review still says reduce. That makes no\nsense to me.\n\n**Store operations lead:** Stores say shelves are empty by early evening. The availability KPI in LEAN stores dropped\nafter go-live.\n\n**Finance transformation:** Shelf stock in LEAN stores is down by more than half. Sales are down everywhere, and\nDemand Science's own estimate put lost sales at about 2%. The programme works; we want to extend it.\n\n**Forecasting lead:** v4 beats v3 on MAPE. If demand has come down, v4 is simply tracking it.\n\n**Actions:** Demand Science to review demand before the buy plan is locked. The competitor opening near two of our\nstores (field note in `notes/`) also needs to be taken into account.\n# Q3 category review: demand baselines and buy plan\n\nPrepared by Supply Planning from `demandsci review` (release 2.3.1). Periods: before and after the LEAN-26 go-live (2026-06-29).\n\n| Category | Sales per day, change | Baseline pre | Baseline post | Baseline change | Proposed action |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Breakfast cereals | -14.7% | 405 | 314 | -22.5% | reduce |\n| Hot beverages | -29.0% | 357 | 229 | -35.8% | reduce |\n| Household cleaning | -17.9% | 390 | 313 | -19.7% | reduce |\n| Ice cream & frozen desserts | +4.6% | 586 | 555 | -5.3% | reduce |\n| Pasta & sauces | -14.5% | 864 | 721 | -16.5% | reduce |\n| Snacks & crisps | -14.4% | 281 | 208 | -25.8% | reduce |\n| Soft drinks | -16.8% | 253 | 189 | -25.5% | reduce |\n| Soups & broths | -28.6% | 402 | 250 | -37.6% | reduce |\n\n**Proposal:** reduce next quarter's buys in 8 of 8 categories and put the SKUs with the steepest baseline declines forward for range review.\n\nBaselines are computed on clean (stockout-free) non-promotional days, so availability issues are already excluded from the trend.\n# LEAN-26 week-8 readout (Finance Transformation)\n\nWindow: 8 weeks from go-live (2026-06-29 to 2026-08-23) against the 8 weeks before.\n\n| Arm | Stores | Closing shelf stock per store-SKU, change | Sales units, change | Stockout days, pre → post |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| LEAN-26 | 12 | -57.6% | -21.1% | 20% → 47% |\n| Holdout | 4 | -4.5% | -5.7% | 21% → 21% |\n\n- Shelf stock (working capital) fell sharply in LEAN-26 stores.\n- Sales fell in both arms, in line with the category declines in the Q3 review and the lower promotion calendar.\n- More stockout days were expected with leaner shelves; Demand Science estimated lost sales at about 2% of demand\n  in the first four weeks (notebook `lost_sales_quick_estimate.ipynb`).\n- **Recommendation:** extend LEAN-26 to the holdout stores after the Q3 review.\n-- Store operations availability KPI: share of trading store-SKU-days with no out-of-stock during trading hours,\n-- by week and LEAN-26 arm.\nSELECT substr(i.date, 1, 4) || '-W' || strftime('%W', i.date) AS week,\n       p.arm,\n       COUNT(*) AS store_sku_days,\n       1.0 - AVG(CASE WHEN i.on_hand_open = 0 OR EXISTS (\n                   SELECT 1 FROM availability_events e\n                   WHERE e.store_id = i.store_id AND e.sku_id = i.sku_id AND e.event_type = 'out_of_stock'\n                     AND substr(e.event_time, 1, 10) = i.date\n                     AND substr(e.event_time, 12, 5) >= c.open_time AND substr(e.event_time, 12, 5) < c.close_time)\n                 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS in_stock_rate\nFROM inventory_daily i\nJOIN store_calendar c ON c.store_id = i.store_id AND c.date = i.date AND c.status = 'open'\nJOIN programme_assignment p ON p.store_id = i.store_id\nGROUP BY week, p.arm\nORDER BY week, p.arm;\nweek,arm,store_sku_days,in_stock_rate\n2026-W14,holdout,1792,0.8041294642857143\n2026-W14,lean26,5376,0.8078497023809523\n2026-W15,holdout,1792,0.7907366071428572\n2026-W15,lean26,5376,0.8050595238095238\nmarkdown -----\n# LEAN-26: quick lost-sales estimate (first 4 weeks)\n\nDemand Science, July 2026. Fill each stockout day with the store-SKU's average sales on clean days in the same window, then compare with actual sales across LEAN-26 stores.\n\ncode -----\nimport sys, sqlite3\nsys.path.insert(0, '..')\nfrom demandsci import warehouse as wh\ncon = sqlite3.connect('../data/warehouse.sqlite')\nGO_LIVE, END = '2026-06-29', '2026-07-27'\n\ncode -----\nd = wh.trading_days(con).merge(wh.daily_sales(con), how='left', on=['store_id', 'sku_id', 'date'])\nd = d.merge(wh.stockout_days(con).assign(stockout=True), how='left', on=['store_id', 'sku_id', 'date'])\nd['units_sold'] = d['units_sold'].fillna(0); d['stockout'] = d['stockout'].eq(True)\nw = d[(d.arm == 'lean26') & (d.date >= GO_LIVE) & (d.date < END)].copy()\nw = w.join(w[~w.stockout].groupby(['store_id', 'sku_id']).units_sold.mean().rename('clean_mean'), on=['store_id', 'sku_id'])\nfilled = w.units_sold.where(~w.stockout, w[['units_sold', 'clean_mean']].max(axis=1).fillna(w.units_sold))\nprint(f'estimated lost sales: {100 * (1 - w.units_sold.sum() / filled.sum()):.1f}% of demand')\n\nmarkdown -----\nStockouts are frequent (47% of store-SKU-days) but cost only about 2% of demand: most items run out late in the day, after they have already sold a normal day's volume.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7d5e6906-1c76-49be-966f-e01370614c42","uuid":"8fbf1291-2f14-4c13-84b0-5f60f2d237d1","timestamp":"2026-10-01T02:53:52.070Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Field note: competitor opening\n\nFrom: Store operations, south region.\n\nA discount grocer opened on Monday 20 July 2026 within walking distance of S08 and S16. Now I'm writing the replacement demand model."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8954,"cache_read_input_tokens":34512,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":8954,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7d5e6906-1c76-49be-966f-e01370614c42","uuid":"dda9cda5-e115-4f40-9b34-9a464172f7bc","timestamp":"2026-10-01T02:56:29.542Z","request_id":"req_011CfamKf4qnJzsSLmZkWyDZ"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfamKgA5UiTEHfx9MUVVS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0173u5QRHdrZ2VC8CUPZ674K","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/workspace/demandsci/demand.py","content":"\"\"\"Demand history: one row per trading store x SKU x day, with unconstrained (expected) demand.\n\nRecorded sales are censored by empty shelves: once an item sells out, demand for the rest of the trading day is not\nseen. For each store-SKU-day the review therefore works out, minute by minute, when the item was on the shelf during\ntrading hours, and converts that into the share of the day's demand that could be observed (\"exposure\"), using the\nstore's hour-by-hour shopper profile for the day type (weekday / Saturday / Sunday; docs/stores/store_operations.md).\n\nExpected demand for the day is then\n\n    E[D | observed] = sales + E[daily demand rate | observed] * (1 - exposure)\n\nwhere the daily rate follows a multiplicative model fitted on all trading days with exposure offsets (so stockout\ndays inform the fit without biasing it):\n\n    rate = store-SKU level x store-day factor x category-day factor x promotion-event uplift x day noise\n\nwith gamma day noise (negative binomial sales). The posterior of the day's rate combines the model mean with the\nsales actually seen while the item was on the shelf. Days fully on the shelf have exposure 1, so demand = sales.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar\nfrom scipy.special import gammaln\n\nfrom demandsci import warehouse\n\nKEY = [\"store_id\", \"sku_id\", \"date\"]\nHOURS = 24\nMINUTES = HOURS * 60\n\n\ndef _minutes(t: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"'HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS' -> minutes after midnight (float).\"\"\"\n    parts = t.astype(str).str.split(\":\", expand=True)\n    m = parts[0].astype(float) * 60 + parts[1].astype(float)\n    if parts.shape[1] > 2:\n        m = m + parts[2].fillna(0).astype(float) / 60\n    return m.to_numpy()\n\n\ndef _day_type(dates: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:\n    dow = pd.to_datetime(dates).dt.dayofweek.to_numpy()\n    return np.where(dow == 5, 1, np.where(dow == 6, 2, 0))       # 0 weekday, 1 Saturday, 2 Sunday\n\n\ndef _hour_overlap(start: np.ndarray, end: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Fraction of each clock hour covered by [start, end) minutes; shape (n, 24).\"\"\"\n    h0 = np.arange(HOURS)[None, :] * 60.0\n    ov = np.minimum(end[:, None], h0 + 60) - np.maximum(start[:, None], h0)\n    return np.clip(ov, 0, 60) / 60.0\n\n\ndef _exposure_hours(con: sqlite3.Connection, hist: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Per row: open fraction and on-shelf fraction of each clock hour (n x 24).\"\"\"\n    n = len(hist)\n    open_m = _minutes(hist[\"open_time\"])\n    close_m = _minutes(hist[\"close_time\"])\n    close_m = np.where(close_m <= open_m, close_m + MINUTES, close_m).clip(max=MINUTES)\n    opened = _hour_overlap(open_m, close_m)\n\n    inv = pd.read_sql_query(\n        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, date, on_hand_open, delivered_units, delivered_at FROM inventory_daily\", con)\n    inv = hist[KEY].reset_index().merge(inv, on=KEY, how=\"left\")\n    ev = pd.read_sql_query(\n        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, substr(event_time, 1, 10) AS date, event_time, event_type FROM availability_events \"\n        \"WHERE event_type IN ('out_of_stock', 'back_in_stock')\", con)\n    ev = ev.merge(hist[KEY].reset_index(), on=KEY, how=\"inner\")\n    ev[\"t\"] = _minutes(ev[\"event_time\"].str.slice(11))\n    ev[\"state\"] = (ev[\"event_type\"] == \"back_in_stock\").astype(int)\n    # A delivery during trading hours restocks the shelf even if the back-in-stock event is missing.\n    dl = inv[(inv[\"delivered_units\"] > 0) & inv[\"delivered_at\"].notna()].copy()\n    dl[\"t\"] = _minutes(dl[\"delivered_at\"])\n    dl[\"state\"] = 1\n    ev = pd.concat([ev[[\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"]], dl[[\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"]]], ignore_index=True)\n    ev = ev[(ev[\"t\"] > open_m[ev[\"index\"]]) & (ev[\"t\"] < close_m[ev[\"index\"]])]\n    # at equal times, apply restocks after sell-outs\n    ev = ev.sort_values([\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"], kind=\"mergesort\")\n\n    instock0 = (inv.set_index(\"index\").loc[np.arange(n), \"on_hand_open\"].fillna(0).to_numpy() > 0)\n    shelf = opened * instock0[:, None]\n    if len(ev):\n        idx = ev[\"index\"].to_numpy()\n        t = ev[\"t\"].to_numpy()\n        st = ev[\"state\"].to_numpy()\n        # Build in-stock intervals per affected row.\n        rows_s, rows_e, rows_i = [], [], []\n        bounds = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, idx[1:] != idx[:-1], True])\n        for b0, b1 in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):\n            i = idx[b0]\n            state, since = instock0[i], open_m[i]\n            for k in range(b0, b1):\n                if st[k] == 1 and not state:\n                    state, since = True, t[k]\n                elif st[k] == 0 and state:\n                    rows_i.append(i); rows_s.append(since); rows_e.append(t[k])\n                    state = False\n            if state:\n                rows_i.append(i); rows_s.append(since); rows_e.append(close_m[i])\n        affected = np.unique(idx)\n        shelf[affected] = 0.0\n        if rows_i:\n            ri = np.asarray(rows_i)\n            cover = _hour_overlap(np.asarray(rows_s, float), np.asarray(rows_e, float))\n            np.add.at(shelf, ri, cover)\n        shelf = np.minimum(shelf, opened)\n    return opened, shelf\n\n\ndef _hourly_sales(con: sqlite3.Connection, hist: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:\n    sh = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, sku_id, date, hour, units FROM sales_hourly\", con)\n    sh = sh.merge(hist[KEY].reset_index(), on=KEY, how=\"inner\")\n    out = np.zeros((len(hist), HOURS))\n    np.add.at(out, (sh[\"index\"].to_numpy(), sh[\"hour\"].to_numpy().astype(int)), sh[\"units\"].to_numpy(float))\n    return out\n\n\ndef _profiles(sales: np.ndarray, shelf: np.ndarray, opened: np.ndarray, group: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Hourly demand profile per group (store x day type): rank-1 Poisson fit of hourly sales with on-shelf\n    exposure, so hours after a sell-out do not drag the profile down. Returns one profile row per input row.\"\"\"\n    prof = np.zeros_like(sales)\n    pooled = None\n    for g in np.unique(group):\n        m = group == g\n        S, X = sales[m], shelf[m]\n        keep = X.sum(1) > 0\n        S, X = S[keep], X[keep]\n        w = np.where(opened[m].sum(0) > 0, 1.0, 0.0)\n        lam = np.ones(len(S))\n        for _ in range(100):\n            den = X @ w\n            lam = np.where(den > 0, S.sum(1) / np.where(den > 0, den, 1), 0.0)\n            expo = lam @ X\n            w_new = np.where(expo > 0, S.sum(0) / np.where(expo > 0, expo, 1), np.nan)\n            w_new = w_new / np.nansum(w_new)\n            if np.allclose(np.nan_to_num(w_new), np.nan_to_num(w), atol=1e-12, rtol=0):\n                w = w_new\n                break\n            w = w_new\n        prof[m] = np.nan_to_num(w, nan=0.0)\n        prof[m] = np.where(np.isnan(w)[None, :], np.nan, prof[m])\n    # Hours open but never observed for a group: borrow the average shape of the other groups.\n    if np.isnan(prof).any():\n        pooled = np.nanmean(np.where(np.isnan(prof), np.nan, prof), axis=0)\n        pooled = np.nan_to_num(pooled, nan=0.0)\n        prof = np.where(np.isnan(prof), pooled[None, :], prof)\n    return prof\n\n\ndef _fit_rates(df: pd.DataFrame, sold: np.ndarray, expo: np.ndarray, factors: list[str],\n               iters: int = 200, tol: float = 1e-10) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Multiplicative Poisson model sold ~ Poisson(prod(factors) * exposure), fitted by cyclic updates.\n    Returns the full-day mean rate per row.\"\"\"\n    codes = [pd.factorize(df[f], sort=True)[0] for f in factors]\n    vals = [np.ones(c.max() + 1) for c in codes]\n    mu = np.ones(len(df))\n    prev = None\n    for _ in range(iters):\n        for c, v in zip(codes, vals):\n            other = mu / v[c]\n            num = np.bincount(c, weights=sold, minlength=len(v))\n            den = np.bincount(c, weights=other * expo, minlength=len(v))\n            new = np.where(den > 0, num / np.where(den > 0, den, 1), 1.0)\n            if new.max() > 0 and (new == 0).any():\n                pass\n            v[:] = new\n            mu = other * v[c]\n        ll = float(np.sum(sold * np.log(np.where(mu * expo > 0, mu * expo, 1)) - mu * expo))\n        if prev is not None and abs(ll - prev) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(prev)):\n            break\n        prev = ll\n    # Rows whose only informative factors had no exposure can end up with a zero rate although the level is\n    # unknown; such levels are estimated from their own group alone only if they have exposure, so keep as is.\n    return mu\n\n\ndef _dispersion(sold: np.ndarray, mean: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Gamma day-noise shape alpha (NB2) by maximum likelihood; large alpha = Poisson.\"\"\"\n    m = mean > 0\n    y, mu = sold[m], mean[m]\n\n    def nll(la):\n        a = np.exp(la)\n        return -np.sum(gammaln(a + y) - gammaln(a) + a * np.log(a / (a + mu)) + y * np.log(mu / (a + mu)))\n\n    r = minimize_scalar(nll, bounds=(np.log(1e-2), np.log(1e6)), method=\"bounded\", options={\"xatol\": 1e-6})\n    return float(np.exp(r.x))\n\n\ndef build_history(con: sqlite3.Connection, days: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    hist = days.sort_values(KEY).reset_index(drop=True)\n    sales_h = _hourly_sales(con, hist)\n    sold = sales_h.sum(1)\n    hist[\"units_sold\"] = sold.astype(int)\n\n    opened, shelf = _exposure_hours(con, hist)\n    hist[\"day_type\"] = _day_type(hist[\"date\"])\n    group = pd.factorize(hist[\"store_id\"].astype(str) + \"|\" + hist[\"day_type\"].astype(str), sort=True)[0]\n    prof = _profiles(sales_h, shelf, opened, group)\n    open_w = (prof * opened).sum(1)\n    expo = np.where(open_w > 0, (prof * shelf).sum(1) / np.where(open_w > 0, open_w, 1), 0.0).clip(0, 1)\n    hist[\"exposure\"] = expo\n    hist[\"stockout_day\"] = expo < 1 - 1e-12\n\n    hist[\"store_sku\"] = hist[\"store_id\"] + \"|\" + hist[\"sku_id\"]\n    hist[\"store_day\"] = hist[\"store_id\"] + \"|\" + hist[\"date\"]\n    hist[\"cat_day\"] = hist[\"category\"] + \"|\" + hist[\"date\"]\n    hist[\"promo_event\"] = np.where(hist[\"promo\"], hist[\"sku_id\"] + \"|\" + hist[\"promo_id\"].astype(str), \"none\")\n    mu = _fit_rates(hist, sold, expo, [\"store_sku\", \"store_day\", \"cat_day\", \"promo_event\"])\n\n    # Day noise: alpha per category, from all days with some exposure (likelihood uses mean = mu * exposure).\n    alpha = pd.Series(index=hist[\"category\"].unique(), dtype=float)\n    for cat, g in hist.groupby(\"category\"):\n        i = g.index.to_numpy()\n        alpha[cat] = _dispersion(sold[i], mu[i] * expo[i])\n    a = hist[\"category\"].map(alpha).to_numpy()\n\n    post_rate = np.where(mu > 0, (a + sold) / (a / np.where(mu > 0, mu, 1) + expo), 0.0)\n    hist[\"expected_demand\"] = sold + post_rate * (1 - expo)\n    hist[\"lost_units\"] = hist[\"expected_demand\"] - hist[\"units_sold\"]\n    return hist.drop(columns=[\"store_sku\", \"store_day\", \"cat_day\", \"promo_event\"])\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":8954,"cache_read_input_tokens":34512,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":8954,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7d5e6906-1c76-49be-966f-e01370614c42","uuid":"28ddde26-024d-4d95-998a-ce9ffe4d706c","timestamp":"2026-10-01T02:57:05.996Z","request_id":"req_011CfamKf4qnJzsSLmZkWyDZ"}

For each store-SKU-day the review therefore works out, minute by minute, when the item was on the shelf during\ntrading hours, and converts that into the share of the day's demand that could be observed (\"exposure\"), using the\nstore's hour-by-hour shopper profile for the day type (weekday / Saturday / Sunday; docs/stores/store_operations.md).\n\nExpected demand for the day is then\n\n    E[D | observed] = sales + E[daily demand rate | observed] * (1 - exposure)\n\nwhere the daily rate follows a multiplicative model fitted on all trading days with exposure offsets (so stockout\ndays inform the fit without biasing it):\n\n    rate = store-SKU level x store-day factor x category-day factor x promotion-event uplift x day noise\n\nwith gamma day noise (negative binomial sales). The posterior of the day's rate combines the model mean with the\nsales actually seen while the item was on the shelf. Days fully on the shelf have exposure 1, so demand = sales.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar\nfrom scipy.special import gammaln\n\nfrom demandsci import warehouse\n\nKEY = [\"store_id\", \"sku_id\", \"date\"]\nHOURS = 24\nMINUTES = HOURS * 60\n\n\ndef _minutes(t: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"'HH:MM' or 'HH:MM:SS' -> minutes after midnight (float).\"\"\"\n    parts = t.astype(str).str.split(\":\", expand=True)\n    m = parts[0].astype(float) * 60 + parts[1].astype(float)\n    if parts.shape[1] > 2:\n        m = m + parts[2].fillna(0).astype(float) / 60\n    return m.to_numpy()\n\n\ndef _day_type(dates: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:\n    dow = pd.to_datetime(dates).dt.dayofweek.to_numpy()\n    return np.where(dow == 5, 1, np.where(dow == 6, 2, 0))       # 0 weekday, 1 Saturday, 2 Sunday\n\n\ndef _hour_overlap(start: np.ndarray, end: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Fraction of each clock hour covered by [start, end) minutes; shape (n, 24).\"\"\"\n    h0 = np.arange(HOURS)[None, :] * 60.0\n    ov = np.minimum(end[:, None], h0 + 60) - np.maximum(start[:, None], h0)\n    return np.clip(ov, 0, 60) / 60.0\n\n\ndef _exposure_hours(con: sqlite3.Connection, hist: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"Per row: open fraction and on-shelf fraction of each clock hour (n x 24).\"\"\"\n    n = len(hist)\n    open_m = _minutes(hist[\"open_time\"])\n    close_m = _minutes(hist[\"close_time\"])\n    close_m = np.where(close_m <= open_m, close_m + MINUTES, close_m).clip(max=MINUTES)\n    opened = _hour_overlap(open_m, close_m)\n\n    inv = pd.read_sql_query(\n        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, date, on_hand_open, delivered_units, delivered_at FROM inventory_daily\", con)\n    inv = hist[KEY].reset_index().merge(inv, on=KEY, how=\"left\")\n    ev = pd.read_sql_query(\n        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, substr(event_time, 1, 10) AS date, event_time, event_type FROM availability_events \"\n        \"WHERE event_type IN ('out_of_stock', 'back_in_stock')\", con)\n    ev = ev.merge(hist[KEY].reset_index(), on=KEY, how=\"inner\")\n    ev[\"t\"] = _minutes(ev[\"event_time\"].str.slice(11))\n    ev[\"state\"] = (ev[\"event_type\"] == \"back_in_stock\").astype(int)\n    # A delivery during trading hours restocks the shelf even if the back-in-stock event is missing.\n    dl = inv[(inv[\"delivered_units\"] > 0) & inv[\"delivered_at\"].notna()].copy()\n    dl[\"t\"] = _minutes(dl[\"delivered_at\"])\n    dl[\"state\"] = 1\n    ev = pd.concat([ev[[\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"]], dl[[\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"]]], ignore_index=True)\n    ev = ev[(ev[\"t\"] > open_m[ev[\"index\"]]) & (ev[\"t\"] < close_m[ev[\"index\"]])]\n    # at equal times, apply restocks after sell-outs\n    ev = ev.sort_values([\"index\", \"t\", \"state\"], kind=\"mergesort\")\n\n    instock0 = (inv.set_index(\"index\").loc[np.arange(n), \"on_hand_open\"].fillna(0).to_numpy() > 0)\n    shelf = opened * instock0[:, None]\n    if len(ev):\n        idx = ev[\"index\"].to_numpy()\n        t = ev[\"t\"].to_numpy()\n        st = ev[\"state\"].to_numpy()\n        # 0 weekday, 1 Saturday, 2 Sunday","+","+","+def _hour_overlap(start: np.ndarray, end: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:","+    \"\"\"Fraction of each clock hour covered by [start, end) minutes; shape (n, 24).\"\"\"","+    h0 = np.arange(HOURS)[None, :] * 60.0","+    ov = np.minimum(end[:, None], h0 + 60) - np.maximum(start[:, None], h0)","+    return np.clip(ov, 0, 60) / 60.0","+","+","+def _exposure_hours(con: sqlite3.Connection, hist: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:","+    \"\"\"Per row: open fraction and on-shelf fraction of each clock hour (n x 24).\"\"\"","+    n = len(hist)","+    open_m = _minutes(hist[\"open_time\"])","+    close_m = _minutes(hist[\"close_time\"])","+    close_m = np.where(close_m <= open_m, close_m + MINUTES, close_m).clip(max=MINUTES)","+    opened = _hour_overlap(open_m, close_m)","+","+    inv = pd.read_sql_query(","+        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, date, on_hand_open, delivered_units, delivered_at FROM inventory_daily\", con)","+    inv = hist[KEY].reset_index().merge(inv, on=KEY, how=\"left\")","+    ev = pd.read_sql_query(","+        \"SELECT store_id, sku_id, substr(event_time, 1, 10) AS date, event_time, event_type FROM availability_events \"","+        \"WHERE event_type IN ('out_of_stock', 'back_in_stock')\", con)","+    ev = ev.merge(hist[KEY].reset_index(), on=KEY, how=\"inner\")","+    ev[\"t\"] = _minutes(ev[\"event_time\"].str.slice(11))","+    ev[\"state\"] = (ev[\"event_type\"] == \"back_in_stock\").astype(int)","+    # Build in-stock intervals per affected row.","+        rows_s, rows_e, rows_i = [], [], []","+        bounds = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, idx[1:] != idx[:-1], True])","+        for b0, b1 in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):","+            i = idx[b0]","+            state, since = instock0[i], open_m[i]","+            for k in range(b0, b1):","+                if st[k] == 1 and not state:","+                    state, since = True, t[k]","+                elif st[k] == 0 and state:","+                    rows_i.append(i); rows_s.append(since); rows_e.append(t[k])","+                    state = False","+            if state:","+                rows_i.append(i); rows_s.append(since); rows_e.append(close_m[i])","+        affected = np.unique(idx)","+        shelf[affected] = 0.0","+        if rows_i:","+            ri = np.asarray(rows_i)","+            cover = _hour_overlap(np.asarray(rows_s, float), np.asarray(rows_e, float))","+            np.add.at(shelf, ri, cover)","+        shelf = np.minimum(shelf, opened)","+    return opened, shelf","+","+","+def _hourly_sales(con: sqlite3.Connection, hist: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:","+    sh = pd.read_sql_query(\"SELECT store_id, sku_id, date, hour, units FROM sales_hourly\", con)","+    sh = sh.merge(hist[KEY].reset_index(), on=KEY, how=\"inner\")","+    out = np.zeros((len(hist), HOURS))","+    np.add.at(out, (sh[\"index\"].to_numpy(), sh[\"hour\"].to_numpy().astype(int)), sh[\"units\"].to_numpy(float))","+    return out","+","+","+def _profiles(sales: np.ndarray, shelf: np.ndarray, opened: np.ndarray, group: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:","+    \"\"\"Hourly demand profile per group (store x day type): rank-1 Poisson fit of hourly sales with on-shelf","+    exposure, so hours after a sell-out do not drag the profile down. Returns one profile row per input row.\"\"\"","+    prof = np.zeros_like(sales)","+    pooled = None","+    for g in np.unique(group):","+        m = group == g","+        S, X = sales[m], shelf[m]","+        keep = X.sum(1) > 0","+        S, X = S[keep], X[keep]","+        w = np.where(opened[m].sum(0) > 0, 1.0, 0.0)","+        lam = np.ones(len(S))","+        for _ in range(100):","+ > 0, expo, 1), np.nan)","+            w_new = w_new / np.nansum(w_new)","+            if np.allclose(np.nan_to_num(w_new), np.nan_to_num(w), atol=1e-12, rtol=0):","+                w = w_new","+                break","+            w = w_new","+        prof[m] = np.nan_to_num(w, nan=0.0)","+        prof[m] = np.where(np.isnan(w)[None, :], np.nan, prof[m])","+    # Hours open but never observed for a group: borrow the average shape of the other groups.","+    if np.isnan(prof).any():","+        pooled = np.nanmean(np.where(np.isnan(prof), np.nan, prof), axis=0)","+        pooled = np.nan_to_num(pooled, nan=0.0)","+        prof = np.where(np.isnan(prof), pooled[None, :], prof)","+    return prof","+","+","+def _fit_rates(df: pd.DataFrame, sold: np.ndarray, expo: np.ndarray, factors: list[str],","+               iters: int = 200, tol: float = 1e-10) -> np.ndarray:","+    \"\"\"Multiplicative Poisson model sold ~ Poisson(prod(factors) * exposure), fitted by cyclic updates.","+    Returns the full-day mean rate per row.\"\"\"","+    codes = [pd.factorize(df[f], sort=True)[0] for f in factors]","+    vals = [np.ones(c.max() + 1) for c in codes]","+    mu = np.ones(len(df))","+    prev = None","+    for _ in range(iters):","+        for c, v in zip(codes, vals):","+            other = mu / v[c]","+            num = np.bincount(c, weights=sold, minlength=len(v))","+            den = np.bincount(c, weights=other * expo, minlength=len(v))","+            new = np.where(den > 0, num / np.where(den > 0, den, 1), 1.0)","+            if new.max() > 0 and (new == 0).any():","+                pass","+            v[:] = new","+            mu = other * v[c]","+        ll = float(np.sum(sold * np.log(np.where(mu * expo > 0, mu * expo, 1)) - mu * expo))","+        if prev is not None and abs(ll - prev) <= tol * max(1.0, abs(prev)):","+            break","+        prev = ll","+    # Rows whose only informative factors had no exposure can end up _dispersion(sold: np.ndarray, mean: np.ndarray) -> float:","+    \"\"\"Gamma day-noise shape alpha (NB2) by maximum likelihood; large alpha = Poisson.\"\"\"","+    m = mean > 0","+    y, mu = sold[m], minimize_scalar(nll, bounds=(np.log(1e-2), np.log(1e6)), method=\"bounded\", options={\"xatol\": 1e-6})","+    return float(np.exp(r.x))","+","+"," def build_history(con: sqlite3.Connection, days: group = pd.factorize(hist[\"store_id\"].astype(str) + \"|\" + hist[\"day_type\"].astype(str), sort=True)[0]","+    prof = _profiles(sales_h, shelf, opened, group)","+    open_w = (prof * recorded sales. Days with a stockout are flagged so that baselines can be computed on clean\ndays (see RELEASES.md).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\nfrom demandsci import warehouse\n\nKEY = [\"store_id\", \"sku_id\", \"date\"]\n\n\ndef build_history(con: sqlite3.Connection, days: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    sales = warehouse.daily_sales(con)\n    hist = days.merge(sales, on=KEY, how=\"left\")\n    hist[\"units_sold\"] = hist[\"units_sold\"].fillna(0).astype(int)\n    so = warehouse.stockout_days(con)\n    so[\"stockout_day\"] = True\n    hist = hist.merge(so, on=KEY, how=\"left\")\n    hist[\"stockout_day\"] = hist[\"stockout_day\"].eq(True)\n    hist[\"expected_demand\"] = hist[\"units_sold\"].astype(float)\n    hist[\"lost_units\"] = hist[\"expected_demand\"] - hist[\"units_sold\"]\n    return hist.sort_values(KEY).reset_index(drop=True)\n","userModified":false}}
